fields.meta_title: Daycare Registration Form Builder for Child Care | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a daycare registration form that places each child in a room by age and takes the registration fee when a parent submits. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Daycare Registration Form That Runs Enrollment
fields.hero_description: Build a daycare registration form that places children by birth date and keeps every family in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Collects, and What It Does Next
fields.features_subheading: Each section answers something staff need on a child's first morning, such as who may take them home and what they cannot eat.
fields.feature_1:
Every guardian on the child's record

Collect the child's legal name and birth date, plus the name they go by. Add each parent or guardian with a phone and email, and upload any custody order staff must follow.
fields.feature_2:
An authorized pickup list at the door

Parents name each adult who may collect their child, with that person's relationship and phone number. Teachers open the list on a tablet at pickup and check each adult against it.
fields.feature_3:
Allergies and medicines staff can find

Ask about allergies, daily medicines, dietary limits, and the child's doctor. Each answer sits on the child's card, so a substitute teacher sees a peanut allergy before snack time.
fields.feature_4:
Full-time care or the days a family picks

Offer full-time care or chosen weekdays, such as Tuesdays and Thursdays. Each choice saves to the family's row, so the director can count which children are due in on any morning.
fields.feature_5:
Policies signed on the parent's phone

Show the program's sick-child and late-pickup policies, then ask for a signature. The app captures the e-signature with the date, and each signed copy stays on the child's record.
fields.feature_6:
Source code you can host elsewhere

On paid plans, export the registration app's source code to your GitHub repository. A developer can then host it on other servers or connect it to tools the program already uses.

fields.tab_content_1:
Each child placed in a room by birth date

Bright Fern Early Learning has 8 seats in its infant room and 12 in its toddler room. The form reads each child's birth date and places them in the right room. When the infant room fills, the next family goes to its waitlist, and the director sees both rooms on one screen.
fields.tab_content_2:
With $75 paid, the spot is held

Marisol Ferreira-Holt cares for 6 children in her home. A parent registers on a phone and pays her $75 registration fee through her Stripe account before the form submits. The payment holds the child's spot, and each family's row shows the fee as paid, with the date.
fields.tab_content_3:
Before day one, the missing record is requested

Otis Beaumont-Kerr starts at Quill Hollow Preschool on Monday, Nov 2. His form came in complete except for the immunization record. On Oct 19, 14 days before his first day, the app emails his mother, Leah Beaumont-Kerr, a link to upload it to his file.
fields.tab_content_4:
For returning families, last year's answers come back

Every March, the 40 families at Cobblestone Child Care re-register for the next school year. Each form opens with last year's answers filled in, and a parent confirms them or changes what is new. The director's list shows 31 families done, and the other 9 get an email reminder every Monday until they finish.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Daycare Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a daycare registration form around your rooms and records, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the child and each guardian
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Add an upload for each record
fields.howto_step_1_des: List each room with the ages it takes and the number of seats it has. Decide what a family sees when its room is full, such as a waitlist place or a later start date. The form uses those numbers for every placement.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the child's details first, then each parent or guardian. Mark one guardian as the first call when a child gets sick at noon, and collect a work phone as well as a mobile number for every guardian on the form.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add an upload field for each record your program keeps on file, such as the immunization record and a doctor's note. Ask for the date on each one. The app can then show which records are missing or out of date before a child starts.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep emergency contacts and the pickup list as two separate questions. A neighbor who can be called when a parent is unreachable is not always someone the parent allows to take the child home, and staff need to see that difference.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the schedule and the fee
fields.howto_step_5_des: Offer the schedules you run, full-time or set weekdays, and show the price of each. If you charge a registration fee, connect the payment tool you already use through its API and take the fee before the form submits.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before you publish, check your state's licensing requirements and compare your fields with any registration form your licensing agency issues. Add the questions it asks that yours does not, and keep the agency's wording for those questions.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Describe it, then register a test child
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the form to Emergent in plain English, with your rooms, fee, and records. Emergent builds the form and its database. Register a test child with a missing record into a full room, then check the waitlist and the reminder.

faq_plan.q: What is a daycare registration form?
faq_plan.a: A daycare registration form is what a family fills in to enroll a child in a child care program. It records the child, the parents or guardians, the adults allowed to pick up, health details, and the schedule. Daycare registration forms give staff one record to check on a child's first morning.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a daycare registration form?
faq_plan.a: Decide your rooms and your fee first, then describe the form in plain English to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form, its database, and the logic that places each child, and you change any of it by prompting. Then send the link to one family you know well and fix whatever confuses them.

faq_plan.q: Can I start from a daycare registration form template?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A daycare registration form template is a useful checklist of fields, and you can paste its questions into your description. Then decide what the form should do after a parent submits, such as placing the child or taking the fee. Emergent builds those steps from the same plain-English prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can one daycare registration form cover after-school care and summer weeks?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the form asks for the program first and shows only the questions that program needs. Questions about naps or bottles can stay hidden for a 7-year-old, for example. When summer runs as its own camp with weekly sessions and separate fees, a summer camp registration form keeps that roster apart from the daycare one.

faq_plan.q: Which documents should a daycare registration form ask parents to upload?
faq_plan.a: Start with the documents your licensing agency names, and check your state's licensing requirements for that list. Then add what your own policies call for, such as the immunization record, a doctor's note for any medicine staff give, or a photo of each pickup adult.

faq_plan.q: What should a daycare registration form do when a room is full?
faq_plan.a: It should tell the family right away and add them to a waitlist. Decide the waitlist order before registration opens, such as by date, with siblings of enrolled children first. When a seat opens, the app can email the next family an offer that expires after 48 hours.

faq_plan.q: Can parents register siblings on one daycare registration form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a repeating child section: the parent's details go in once, and each child gets a birth date and health details of their own. It works like adding attendees on a conference registration form, where one person signs up several people in a single submission.

faq_plan.q: How often should families update their daycare registration form?
faq_plan.a: Set one yearly date for every family to review the whole form, then check your state's licensing requirements in case they ask for more. Between those dates, let parents change a phone number or a pickup adult the day it changes. With Emergent, those answers live in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can parents fill out daycare registration forms on their phones?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The form Emergent builds is a web page, and parents open it from a link in a text or an email. If you keep a daycare registration form PDF for families who prefer paper, type those answers into the same form to keep one roster. There are no response caps, however many families register in the first week.

faq_plan.q: What should happen after a family submits a daycare registration form?
faq_plan.a: Send a confirmation right away with the child's room, start date, and anything still missing, and alert the director to the new family. A general registration form can stop at a thank-you page. A daycare one should walk the family toward their first morning.

plan.angle: Five of the top 10 are state child-care licensing PDFs, and Jotform plus one enrollment-forms vendor hold the template slots. Each of those is a list of fields that ends when a parent signs. This page says what a daycare registration form has to ask (the child, the parents, who may pick up, health details, the schedule and the fee), tells the reader to check their state's licensing requirements rather than copying one state's PDF, and then shows the form as a working enrollment app: a center placing children in rooms by birth date, a home provider taking the fee at submit, a preschool chasing a missing immunization record before day one, and a program running yearly re-registration for returning families.
